title: wasm : update and fix examples
body:
The Emscripten build for the WASM examples hasn't been maintained for a very long time. There are likely regressions that have been introduced that would need to be fixed.

Last working examples: https://<redacted-host>

- Fix WASM builds
- Update instructions
- Add CI workflows
- Host the WASM examples on a new domain and update regularly

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: There seems to be a problem with the WASM example - when I transcribe longer audio using the `tiny` model, the processing often stops without any error or notification: @participant2 Can you reproduce on your end? I am usually able to reproduce by running `gb0.wav` or `gb1.wav` from the samples, using 8 threads in a Chrome browser.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
> [@participant2](https://github.com/participant2) Can you reproduce on your end?

I'll take a look 👍 I've only been testing with the sample jfk.wav which is pretty short.

comments.author: participant2
reporter
comments.body:
Try using the `tiny.en (75 MB)` model. Here are the samples:

[gb0.wav.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/19581351/gb0.wav.txt)

[gb1.wav.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/19581358/gb1.wav.txt)

(remove the `.txt` extension)

I am able to reproduce this only in Chrome by transcribing the 2 samples one after the other. Eventually it hangs. I also reproduce it with the old WASM examples at: https://<redacted-host>, so it is not a new issue.

The strange thing is that it does not happen neither in Safari, nor in Firefox.

Btw, I just noticed the "unknown language" error when using non-en models. This looks like a separate issue.

Ah good to know that, as it might not be cause by the changes to the WebAssembly memory setting in emscripten we made.

I noticed this as well for the none `.en` models. I'll take a look at that too.
